scenes.tts: If microglia eat retinal inputs, can we catch them doing it? And do they choose what they eat?
scenes.visual: Title card: Caught in the Act. A green microglial cell among red and blue axons.
scenes.narration: If microglia eat retinal inputs, can we catch them doing it? And do they choose what they eat?

scenes.tts: In twenty twelve, Dorothy Schafer, in the Stevens laboratory, set out to look.
scenes.visual: Credit: Schafer and colleagues, Stevens laboratory, 2012.
scenes.caption: In 2012, Dorothy Schafer, in the Stevens laboratory, set out to look.
scenes.narration: In 2012, Dorothy Schafer, in the Stevens laboratory, set out to look.

scenes.tts: Each eye got its own colored tracer at postnatal day four. A day later, they looked in the visual thalamus.
scenes.visual: Red tracer into one eye, blue into the other, labelled P4; then the dLGN at P5.
scenes.narration: Each eye got its own colored tracer at postnatal day four. A day later, they looked in the visual thalamus.

scenes.tts: A speck beside a microglial cell does not show it was eaten. So only label inside the cell counts.
scenes.visual: A green microglial cell rebuilt in 3D; specks outside its outline fade away, specks inside stay. On screen: engulfment index (%) = volume of retinal label inside the microglial cell ÷ volume of that microglial cell × 100.
scenes.narration: A speck beside a microglial cell does not show it was eaten. So only label inside the cell counts.

scenes.tts: Retinal material sat inside microglial lysosomes, the cell's digestive compartments. A dye that glows only in acid agreed.
scenes.visual: Specks inside a lysosome; the lysosome glows in an acid-reporting color.
scenes.narration: Retinal material sat inside microglial lysosomes, the cell's digestive compartments. A dye that glows only in acid agreed.

scenes.tts: The swallowed material was mainly presynaptic, from retinal terminals.
scenes.visual: A retinal terminal fragment inside the cell, labelled presynaptic.
scenes.narration: The swallowed material was mainly presynaptic, from retinal terminals.

scenes.tts: Eating had a clock. It was high at postnatal day five, and much lower by day nine.
scenes.visual: Two bars labelled schematic: P5 high, P9 much lower.
scenes.narration: Eating had a clock. It was high at postnatal day five, and much lower by day nine.

scenes.tts: Eating also used a tag and a reader. Without complement receptor three, the reader, or C three, the tag's source, microglia took up about half as much.
scenes.visual: Bars: normal, CR3 knockout, C3 knockout; the knockouts at about half. Labelled schematic.
scenes.caption: Eating also used a tag and a reader. Without complement receptor 3, the reader, or C3, the tag's source, microglia took up about half as much.
scenes.narration: Eating also used a tag and a reader. Without complement receptor 3, the reader, or C3, the tag's source, microglia took up about half as much.

scenes.tts: Those mice later had more overlap between the eye territories, and extra retinal synapses.
scenes.visual: The knockout dLGN shows a purple overlap zone; a synapse count tile reads: more, about one month.
scenes.narration: Those mice later had more overlap between the eye territories, and extra retinal synapses.

scenes.tts: But half the eating remained. Complement is one route of several.
scenes.visual: The remaining half of the bar is highlighted: other routes.
scenes.narration: But half the eating remained. Complement is one route of several.

scenes.tts: Now the key question. Silence one eye with tetrodotoxin, which blocks sodium channels.
scenes.visual: One eye darkens; label: tetrodotoxin (TTX), silenced. The other eye gets a matched control injection.
scenes.narration: Now the key question. Silence one eye with tetrodotoxin, which blocks sodium channels.

scenes.tts: Predict. If microglia remove less active inputs, whose material should they hold more of?
scenes.visual: Question card held over the microglial cell with red and blue specks.
scenes.narration: Predict. If microglia remove less active inputs, whose material should they hold more of?

scenes.tts: More of the silenced eye's material, relative to how much of that eye's input is there.
scenes.visual: Two separate bars, each eye's engulfed label divided by that eye's local labelled input; the silenced-eye bar is higher. Raw colour shares are not shown. Label: per unit of that eye's input. Schematic.
scenes.narration: More of the silenced eye's material, relative to how much of that eye's input is there.

scenes.tts: Boost one eye with forskolin instead, and they take relatively more of the untreated eye's.
scenes.visual: One eye brightens; label: forskolin, more active. Two normalized bars again, per unit of each eye's input; now the untreated eye's bar is higher. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Boost one eye with forskolin instead, and they take relatively more of the untreated eye's.

scenes.tts: The two drugs push in opposite directions. A drug that simply damaged axons would raise eating of its own eye both times.
scenes.visual: Two arrows pointing opposite ways, labelled TTX and forskolin.
scenes.narration: The two drugs push in opposite directions. A drug that simply damaged axons would raise eating of its own eye both times.

scenes.tts: Why relative to what is there? Near one microglial cell, one eye's input can far outnumber the other's.
scenes.visual: A small sampling circle around one microglial cell; inside it, many red terminals and few blue. Label: local input, 90 units and 10 units (invented numbers).
scenes.narration: Why relative to what is there? Near one microglial cell, one eye's input can far outnumber the other's.

scenes.tts: Say ninety units from one eye, and ten from the other. An eater with no preference takes a tenth of each, so it holds nine to one.
scenes.visual: No-preference cell: 9 units red, 1 unit blue inside it. On screen: takes 0.1 of each eye's input. Invented numbers.
scenes.narration: Say 90 units from one eye, and 10 from the other. An eater with no preference takes a tenth of each, so it holds 9 to 1.
scenes.caption: Say 90 units from one eye, and 10 from the other. An eater with no preference takes a tenth of each, so it holds 9 to 1.

scenes.tts: Now silence the minor eye, and let the eater take twice the fraction of it: two tenths instead of one tenth. It holds two units, still fewer than nine.
scenes.visual: Blue, silenced: 2 of 10 units eaten (0.2). Red: 9 of 90 units eaten (0.1). Raw bars: blue still smaller. Per-unit bars: blue twice as high. Invented numbers.
scenes.caption: Now silence the minor eye, and let the eater take twice the fraction of it: two tenths instead of one tenth. It holds 2 units, still fewer than 9.
scenes.narration: Now silence the minor eye, and let the eater take twice the fraction of it: two tenths instead of one tenth. It holds 2 units, still fewer than 9.

scenes.tts: So a fair test compares each eye with its own input, measured where the microglia are sampled.
scenes.visual: Card: compare each eye with its own local input. A whole-nucleus map cannot give the local numbers.
scenes.narration: So a fair test compares each eye with its own input, measured where the microglia are sampled.

scenes.tts: Now the limits. This compares whole eyes, not single synapses. It does not show how activity becomes a mark. And later imaging elsewhere suggests microglia often take bites, not whole synapses.
scenes.visual: Limits list builds: whole eyes, not single synapses; how activity becomes a mark, open; bites, not whole synapses (other preparations).
scenes.narration: Now the limits. This compares whole eyes, not single synapses. It does not show how activity becomes a mark. And later imaging elsewhere suggests microglia often take bites, not whole synapses.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea again. Relative activity biases how much material microglia take from each eye. Complement helps them take part of it. How the two connect is still open.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: activity biases how much microglia take from each eye; complement helps them take part of it. The words biases and part underlined; a gap between the two halves labelled: open.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea again. Relative activity biases how much material microglia take from each eye. Complement helps them take part of it. How the two connect is still open.
